# AI Use Log

This log records uses of AI that influenced my portfolio.

## Section 1

**Tool used:** Claude (Anthropic)

Claude was used throughout Section 1 primarily as a learning and coding support tool. I used it to clarify concepts from the lecture notes, check my exercise answers, translate mathematical formulations into LaTeX, and help implement methods in R where I had first worked through the underlying formulas or pseudocode myself. It was also used to explain unfamiliar R functions and model output, and to assist with formatting my Section 1 workthrough.

### Interactive revision material

I asked Claude to create interactive HTML revision files from the Section 1 notes. These summarised the key concepts and included questions that I could work through before revealing the answers.

-   [Section 1A: Chapters 1--6](section-1/S1_Chapters_1-6.html){target="_blank"}
-   [Section 1B: Conditional Variance Models](section-1/S1_Conditional_Variance_Models.html){target="_blank"}
-   [Section 1C: Spectral Analysis](section-1/S1_Spectral_Analysis.html){target="_blank"}
-   [Section 1 workthrough](section-1/section-1.qmd){target="_blank"}

::: ai-log-table
| AI-assisted area                                 | How Claude was used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | What I checked or did myself                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Conceptual explanations**                      | Claude was used to clarify concepts that I did not initially understand, including missing data in discrete and continuous time series, different realisations of a stochastic process, the frequency-domain view of a series, conditional variance models and spectral analysis. | I checked explanations against the lecture notes and used follow-up questions where necessary until I could explain and apply the concepts myself. |
| **Mathematical notation and model formulations** | Claude helped format model definitions and derivations in LaTeX and made the notation in my workthrough more consistent.                                                                                                                                                          | I checked the equations against the formulations in the notes before including them.                                                               |
| **R implementation and exercises**               | Claude helped explain R functions and translate methods or pseudocode into R while I worked through the Section 1 exercises and tutorials.                                                                                                                                        | I ran all code myself and checked the results against the theory, lecture material and expected model behaviour.                                   |
| **Conditional variance models**                  | Claude explained ADF and KPSS testing, how to use the relevant R functions, how to interpret GARCH output, and helped write code for extracting model-selection quantities such as AIC and BIC.                                                                                   | I ran the tests and models myself and interpreted the results in the context of the exercises and lecture material.                                |
| **Spectral analysis**                            | Claude walked through the provided Spectral Analysis R tutorial line by line and explained concepts such as the Nyquist frequency and how to interpret a periodogram.                                                                                                             | I checked that I could interpret the output myself and used the lecture notes or other course material where an AI explanation was insufficient.   |
| **Interactive revision files**                   | Claude converted the lecture material into the three interactive HTML revision resources linked above, including summaries and self-test questions.                                                                                                                               | I checked the content against the notes and attempted the questions before viewing the answers.                                                    |
:::

## Section 2

**Tool used:** Claude (Anthropic)

Claude was used in Section 2 in a similar way to Section 1: primarily to help me understand new modelling frameworks, translate mathematical procedures or pseudocode into R, debug implementations and create interactive revision resources. Because Section 2 involved more algorithmic methods, particularly state-space models and Hidden Markov Models, I also used Claude to step through algorithms and explain how the mathematical formulation related to the code.

### Interactive revision material

I asked Claude to create interactive HTML revision files from the Section 2 material, using the same approach as for Section 1. These were used as supplementary revision resources rather than replacements for the lecture notes.

-   [Section 2: Exponential Smoothing](section-2/S2_Exponential_Smoothing.html){target="_blank"}
-   [Section 2: State-Space Models](section-2/S2_State_Space_Models.html){target="_blank"}
-   [Section 2: Regression](section-2/S2-Regression.html){target="_blank"}
-   [Section 2: Hidden Markov Models](section-2/S2_Hidden_Markov_Models.html){target="_blank"}

::: ai-log-table
| AI-assisted area                      | How Claude was used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | What I checked or did myself                                                                                                                                                      |
|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Conceptual explanations**           | Claude was used to clarify the relationship between exponential smoothing and state-space models, the role of observed and latent states, and how the different Section 2 modelling frameworks were connected.                                            | I checked the explanations against the lecture material and made sure I could interpret the models independently before applying them.                                            |
| **Exponential smoothing**             | Claude helped connect the exponential-smoothing recursions to their state-space representation and assisted with coding implementations based on pseudocode.                                                                                              | I checked the recursions against the model formulation, ran the implementations and compared their behaviour with package-based results where appropriate.                        |
| **State-space models and filtering**  | Claude was used to step through state-space notation and filtering procedures and to explain how sequential updating works computationally.                                                                                                               | I worked through the calculations and checked that I understood the interpretation of the latent state, prediction and updating steps rather than relying only on generated code. |
| **Regression and time-series errors** | Claude assisted with explanations and implementation details where regression was combined with time-series structure, including how predictors and serial dependence should be handled.                                                                  | I checked model specifications and output against the lecture material and interpreted the fitted relationships myself.                                                           |
| **Hidden Markov Models**              | Claude explained the main HMM components and algorithms, including the forward recursion and Viterbi algorithm, and helped translate pseudocode into reusable R functions. This later formed the basis of the first-principles toolkit used in Project 4. | I checked the functions against the HMM equations and validated the implementation against package-based results where possible.                                                  |
| **HMM software and diagnostics**      | Claude helped explain how to use `depmixS4`, fit models with different numbers of regimes, work with multiple starting values, assess parameter precision and implement model diagnostics such as pseudo-residuals.                                       | I ran and compared the models myself, investigated poor solutions and used the statistical output and diagnostics to make the final modelling decisions.                          |
| **Code debugging and streamlining**   | Claude assisted with debugging and reorganising repeated Section 2 code into clearer functions and workflows, particularly for algorithms that were later reused in Project 4.                                                                            | I checked that refactoring did not change the numerical results and retained responsibility for the final implementations.                                                        |
| **Interactive revision files**        | Claude generated the four Section 2 HTML revision resources linked above from the course material, including summaries and questions for self-testing.                                                                                                    | I checked the material against the notes and used the resources to test and clarify my understanding.                                                                             |
:::

# Portfolio Projects

## Portfolio-wide AI assistance

In addition to the project-specific uses documented below, Claude (Anthropic) was used throughout the portfolio for spell-checking, grammar and wording improvements, LaTeX and Quarto formatting, and periodic checks against the portfolio guidelines. Statistical interpretations and final modelling decisions remained my responsibility.

## Project 1

**Tool used:** Claude (Anthropic)

::: ai-log-table
| AI-assisted task                                  | How Claude was used                                                                                                                                                           | What I checked or did myself                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Data-access instructions**                      | Claude helped me locate and understand how to access the electricity-demand data required for the project.                                                                    | I accessed the data myself, checked that the required period and variables were present and documented the data source used in the project.                                                                  |
| **Reading the data into R**                       | Claude assisted with the R code required to import the data, parse dates and place the series into a form suitable for time-series analysis.                                  | I ran the import code, checked the date range, observation frequency and resulting values against the source data.                                                                                           |
| **Initial data-quality checks**                   | Claude helped write code to check missing observations, duplicated dates/observations and other basic data-quality issues.                                                    | I inspected the identified issues and decided how they should be handled before modelling.                                                                                                                   |
| **Plotting code**                                 | Claude assisted with all major plotting code, including time-series plots, decompositions, diagnostic plots and forecast/evaluation figures.                                  | I decided what needed to be visualised, checked the plotted values and edited labels, annotations and presentation where required.                                                                           |
| **Structural-break testing**                      | I asked Claude to explain how a structural-break test could be implemented for the electricity-demand series.                                                                 | I used the test as supporting evidence rather than treating the estimated break dates as automatically correct, and interpreted the break in the context of the COVID-19 period and the modelling objective. |
| **Stepping through structural-break pseudocode**  | Claude helped me work through the structural-break procedure step by step and translate the required workflow into R code.                                                    | I ran the procedure, inspected the candidate break dates and compared them with the observed series and relevant dates.                                                                                      |
| **Strengthening the structural-break assessment** | Claude suggested checking multiple values of the minimum segment length / trimming parameter rather than relying on one setting.                                              | I ran the alternative specifications and used the sensitivity of the estimated break dates as part of my decision about the training period.                                                                 |
| **Holt--Winters from first principles**           | I supplied the Holt--Winters formulas/pseudocode and asked Claude to help translate the recursions into an R implementation from first principles.                            | I checked each recursion against the model definition, compared the behaviour with package-based exponential-smoothing output and interpreted the fitted components myself.                                  |
| **Rolling-window evaluation**                     | Claude helped write reusable model-fitting and forecasting functions so that several models could be evaluated consistently over rolling/expanding forecast origins.          | I determined the training, validation and test design, checked that each forecast used only information available at the forecast origin and interpreted the resulting errors.                               |
| **`imap()` / `purrr` workflow**                   | Claude explained how `imap()` could be used to streamline repeated fitting or forecasting across named model specifications and helped adapt my code to use it.               | I checked that each model name was correctly matched to its forecast output and that the streamlined workflow reproduced the original calculations.                                                          |
| **Diebold--Mariano test**                         | Claude explained the purpose of the Diebold--Mariano test and assisted with the R implementation for comparing forecast accuracy.                                             | I selected the forecasts/losses being compared and interpreted the test in conjunction with the observed forecast errors rather than using the p-value alone.                                                |
| **Empirical prediction intervals**                | Claude helped me check the construction of empirical prediction intervals based on forecast/residual errors and identify issues with how the intervals were being calculated. | I checked interval coverage and width against the observed holdout values and discussed the limitations of constructing intervals from the available residual information.                                   |
| **Annual-cycle adjustment**                       | After comparing model behaviour, Claude suggested testing whether removing the additional annual-cycle adjustment simplified or improved the forecasting approach.            | I compared the competing specifications using the validation/test framework and made the final modelling decision based on the evaluation results.                                                           |
| **Fourier terms for the annual cycle**            | Claude helped write a function to generate the required sine and cosine Fourier terms for an annual cycle.                                                                    | I checked the frequencies/periods used, inspected the generated terms and assessed whether adding them improved forecast performance.                                                                        |
| **Inline values**                                 | Claude helped write inline R expressions so numerical results in the text were populated directly from fitted objects and evaluation results.                                 | I checked the rendered values against the underlying R objects.                                                                                                                                              |
| **Table formatting**                              | Claude assisted with formatting all result and diagnostic tables for the rendered portfolio.                                                                                  | I checked that the values, labels, units and captions agreed with the analysis output.                                                                                                                       |
:::

### AI errors identified and corrected

::: ai-log-table
| Issue identified                           | What was wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | How it was corrected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Comparison with `depmixS4`**             | The original text stated that `depmixS4` "agreed closely" with my first-principles toolkit. On closer inspection, the default `depmixS4` fit had effectively collapsed to a one-state solution, so this comparison was misleading.                                                                      | I refitted `depmixS4` using both its default starting values and selected starting values, compared the resulting likelihoods and state parameters, and revised the discussion to explain the collapsed default solution explicitly.                                   |
| **HMM versus GARCH volatility comparison** | I initially compared HMM volatility constructed from **smoothed** state probabilities with GARCH volatility. Smoothed probabilities use observations from the future, whereas the GARCH volatility forecast at time (t) only uses information available up to that point, making the comparison unfair. | I replaced the primary comparison with HMM volatility based on **filtered** probabilities so that both methods use only information available at the time. The smoothed-probability result is still reported separately as a retrospective description of the regimes. |
| **Single set of HMM starting values**      | The HMMs were initially fitted from only one set of starting values. Because the HMM likelihood can contain local optima, convergence from one start did not provide enough evidence that the fitted solution was the best available one.                                                               | I added five random initialisations for each model specification and retained the fit with the highest attained log-likelihood. The final discussion now acknowledges the sensitivity of HMM optimisation to starting values.                                          |
:::

## Responsibility for AI-assisted work

All AI-assisted code and output were run and checked by me. Where appropriate, I compared implementations with lecture material, model definitions, diagnostics or package-based results. Claude was used to accelerate coding, debugging, formatting and understanding, but I remained responsible for the final modelling decisions, statistical interpretations and material included in the portfolio.
